missions.title: The Festival Storybook Rescue
missions.learning_focus: Story grammar; sequential plot; main idea; collective/concrete/abstract nouns; demonstrative and relative pronouns; verb-forming suffixes; helping/linking/transitive verbs; noun complements; narrative text; layout, tone, and mood.
missions.story_premise: On the morning of Bayang Haraya’s Freedom and Friendship Festival, the town storybook loses its first chapter. Farmer Lira remembers pieces of the parade story, but the Haze has scattered the events, captions, and illustrations across three connected festival zones. The Pathfinder must restore the chapter in correct order before the opening ceremony.
missions.mission_objective: Complete the three connected areas and apply the mission learning focus: Story grammar; sequential plot; main idea; collective/concrete/abstract nouns; demonstrative and relative pronouns; verb-forming suffixes; helping/linking/transitive verbs; noun complements; narrative text; layout, tone, and mood.

areas.title: Parade Meadow
areas.story: Farmer Lira asks the Pathfinder to repair the opening section of the festival chapter. The learner observes a short illustrated scene, identifies the character, setting, goal, and first event, then repairs banner captions using clear noun and pronoun references. The repaired banner route opens the path deeper into the festival and reveals Story Fragment 1.

opening_dialogue.speaker: Farmer Lira
opening_dialogue.text: Pathfinder, the opening of our festival story is missing.

opening_dialogue.speaker: Farmer Lira
opening_dialogue.text: Read the picture and the surviving lines. Find who is here, where they are, what they want to do, and what happened first.

opening_dialogue.speaker: Farmer Lira
opening_dialogue.text: Then repair the banner captions so every noun and pronoun points clearly to the right person or object.

learning_clues: Story grammar identifies character, setting, goal, and events.
A pronoun must clearly refer to a noun already named.

questions.prompt: Who asks the Pathfinder to restore the opening page?
questions.first_wrong_hint: Look at the first sentence of the story source.
questions.second_wrong_explanation: Farmer Lira is standing beside the storybook and asks for help.
questions.correct_feedback: Farmer Lira is standing beside the storybook and asks for help.

questions.prompt: Where does the opening event happen?

options.text: At Parade Meadow near the old acacia tree

questions.first_wrong_hint: Find the place named in the opening page.
questions.second_wrong_explanation: The setting is Parade Meadow near the old acacia tree.
questions.correct_feedback: The setting is Parade Meadow near the old acacia tree.

questions.prompt: What do the children plan to do?

options.text: Carry a friendship banner to Freedom Stage

questions.first_wrong_hint: Look for the children’s goal.
questions.second_wrong_explanation: Their goal is to carry the friendship banner to Freedom Stage.
questions.correct_feedback: Their goal is to carry the friendship banner to Freedom Stage.

questions.prompt: Which event happens first?

options.text: The children gather near the old acacia tree.
The completed chapter is placed in the Chronicle.

questions.first_wrong_hint: Use the sequence in the story source.
questions.second_wrong_explanation: The children gathering is the first stated event.
questions.correct_feedback: The children gathering is the first stated event.

questions.prompt: In “They plan to carry a friendship banner,” who does “They” refer to?
questions.first_wrong_hint: Find the plural noun immediately before the pronoun.
questions.second_wrong_explanation: “They” clearly refers to the children.
questions.correct_feedback: “They” clearly refers to the children.

areas.world_action: Place the correct opening caption and pronoun labels on the parade board.
areas.world_result: The parade board becomes readable, the banner route repairs itself, and Story Fragment 1 appears.
areas.story_source: Farmer Lira stands beside the town storybook at Parade Meadow. The opening page shows children gathering near the old acacia tree. They plan to carry a friendship banner to Freedom Stage, but the first caption has vanished.

areas.title: Drumbeat Lane
areas.story: The parade has lost its written rhythm and its lantern poster communicates the wrong mood. The learner restores action instructions using appropriate verb forms and complements, compares visual layouts and tone, and chooses evidence that supports the intended meaning. The corrected drum-and-lantern sequence reveals Story Fragment 2.

opening_dialogue.speaker: Mina
opening_dialogue.text: The action words are back, but the rhythm instructions and lantern poster still send mixed messages.

opening_dialogue.speaker: Mina
opening_dialogue.text: Check how each verb works, complete the missing complement, and choose the layout that matches a warm, welcoming festival.

learning_clues: Helping verbs work with a main verb; linking verbs connect a subject to a description; transitive verbs act on an object.
Layout, color, images, and spacing help communicate tone and mood.

questions.prompt: Which word is the helping verb in “The drummers are practicing”?
questions.first_wrong_hint: The helping verb comes before the main action verb.
questions.second_wrong_explanation: “Are” helps the main verb “practicing.”
questions.correct_feedback: “Are” helps the main verb “practicing.”

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses a linking verb?
questions.first_wrong_hint: A linking verb connects the subject to a description.
questions.second_wrong_explanation: “Look” links “lanterns” to the description “bright.”
questions.correct_feedback: “Look” links “lanterns” to the description “bright.”

questions.prompt: In “Mina carries the lead drum,” what receives the action?
questions.first_wrong_hint: A transitive verb has an object that receives the action.
questions.second_wrong_explanation: The lead drum receives the action of “carries.”
questions.correct_feedback: The lead drum receives the action of “carries.”

questions.prompt: Which word completes what Lino became in “The crowd named Lino the parade ___”?
questions.first_wrong_hint: The missing word names the role given to Lino.
questions.second_wrong_explanation: “Leader” completes the meaning of what Lino was named.
questions.correct_feedback: “Leader” completes the meaning of what Lino was named.

questions.prompt: Which poster design best matches a friendly festival?

options.text: Open spacing, warm colors, smiling people, and a clear title
Dark crowded images and a warning-style title

questions.first_wrong_hint: Choose visual elements that support a welcoming tone.
questions.second_wrong_explanation: Warm, clear, relevant visuals support the intended friendly mood.
questions.correct_feedback: Warm, clear, relevant visuals support the intended friendly mood.

areas.world_action: Repair the drum instructions and replace the misleading poster with the welcoming layout.
areas.world_result: The drums regain their rhythm, the lanterns glow warmly, and Story Fragment 2 appears.
areas.story_source: At Drumbeat Lane, a sign reads: “The drummers are practicing. Mina carries the lead drum. The lanterns look bright, and the crowd named Lino the parade leader.” A second poster uses dark crowded images that make the friendly celebration look frightening.

areas.title: Freedom Stage
areas.story: At the final stage, the learner arranges seven illustrated events into a coherent narrative, selects the best title and main idea, and completes a short ending. The integrated final challenge reuses the strongest story-grammar, language, and visual-literacy concepts from the mission. The restored festival chapter reveals Story Fragment 3 and completes the mission.

opening_dialogue.speaker: Festival Keeper
opening_dialogue.text: The final page will appear only when the seven events form one clear narrative.

opening_dialogue.speaker: Festival Keeper
opening_dialogue.text: Arrange the events, choose the main idea and title, then complete an ending that fits the story’s hopeful mood.

learning_clues: A coherent narrative has a logical beginning, middle, and ending.
The main idea tells what the whole story is mostly about; a title should match it.

questions.prompt: Which event belongs first?

options.text: The children gather at the acacia tree.
The community carries the finished chapter to the stage.

questions.first_wrong_hint: Start with the event that introduces the characters and setting.
questions.second_wrong_explanation: The gathering at the acacia tree begins the sequence.
questions.correct_feedback: The gathering at the acacia tree begins the sequence.

questions.prompt: Which event happens immediately after the parade captions are restored?
questions.first_wrong_hint: Use the numbered event evidence.
questions.second_wrong_explanation: The repaired captions cause the banner route to open.
questions.correct_feedback: The repaired captions cause the banner route to open.

questions.prompt: What is the best main idea?

options.text: The community restores a damaged festival story by using reading, language, and visual clues.
The festival is canceled because the book is missing.
Only the drummers can repair the town.
The story is mainly about building a laboratory.

questions.first_wrong_hint: Choose the statement that covers the entire mission.
questions.second_wrong_explanation: The mission is about restoring the festival story through evidence-based literacy tasks.
questions.correct_feedback: The mission is about restoring the festival story through evidence-based literacy tasks.

questions.prompt: Which title best matches the completed narrative?
questions.first_wrong_hint: The title should name the central problem and solution.
questions.second_wrong_explanation: “The Festival Storybook Rescue” matches the whole narrative.
questions.correct_feedback: “The Festival Storybook Rescue” matches the whole narrative.

questions.prompt: Which ending best fits the story?

options.text: The restored chapter is read at Freedom Stage, and the community begins the festival together.
The Pathfinder hides the chapter so no one can read it.
The characters forget every repaired event.
The festival changes into an unrelated contest.

questions.first_wrong_hint: Choose an ending that resolves the goal and keeps the hopeful mood.
questions.second_wrong_explanation: The public reading resolves the mission and completes the celebration.
questions.correct_feedback: The public reading resolves the mission and completes the celebration.

areas.world_action: Arrange all seven event cards, bind the three Story Fragments, and place the restored chapter in the Festival Chronicle.
areas.world_result: Freedom Stage lights up, the Chronicle opens, the restored story is read, and the mission completes.
areas.story_source: Seven event cards remain: (1) children gather at the acacia tree; (2) Farmer Lira opens the damaged storybook; (3) the Pathfinder restores the parade captions; (4) the banner route opens; (5) the drummers practice the repaired instructions; (6) the lantern poster is corrected; (7) the community carries the finished chapter to Freedom Stage.

missions.title: The Storm Inside
missions.learning_focus: Recognizing stress and applying healthy coping strategies.
missions.story_premise: A sudden school-festival delay makes Wellness Park glow red. Nico and Maya react differently to stress, and the player helps them choose and apply healthy coping actions.
missions.mission_objective: Complete the three connected areas and apply the mission learning focus: Recognizing stress and applying healthy coping strategies.

areas.title: Signal Garden
areas.story: The learner observes physical, emotional, and behavioral signs of stress, then practices a short paced-breathing response in the same zone. The goal is recognition and a safe first coping action, not diagnosis. A calm change in the garden reveals Wellness Symbol 1.

opening_dialogue.speaker: Health Guide Aya
opening_dialogue.text: These body feelings, thoughts, and behaviors can be signs of stress. They are clues, not a diagnosis.

opening_dialogue.speaker: Health Guide Aya
opening_dialogue.text: Help Nico notice the signs and practice slow breathing before choosing the next step.

learning_clues: Stress can show through body sensations, emotions, thoughts, and behavior.
Slow breathing is one safe coping strategy; persistent or serious distress should be shared with a trusted adult.

questions.prompt: Which detail is a physical sign of stress?
questions.first_wrong_hint: Look for a body sensation.
questions.second_wrong_explanation: Tight shoulders are a physical sign.
questions.correct_feedback: Tight shoulders are a physical sign.

questions.prompt: Which thought may show stress?

options.text: “I will ask what time the program starts.”

questions.first_wrong_hint: Look for the worried prediction.
questions.second_wrong_explanation: The repeated worst-case thought may be a stress sign.
questions.correct_feedback: The repeated worst-case thought may be a stress sign.

questions.prompt: One stress sign is enough to diagnose a health condition.
questions.first_wrong_hint: Signs are clues, not a diagnosis.
questions.second_wrong_explanation: The statement is false. A trusted adult or health professional should handle serious concerns.
questions.correct_feedback: The statement is false. A trusted adult or health professional should handle serious concerns.

questions.prompt: What is a safe first coping action for Nico?

options.text: Pause and take slow, comfortable breaths.

questions.first_wrong_hint: Choose a calm, low-risk action.
questions.second_wrong_explanation: Slow breathing can help Nico pause and settle before deciding what to do next.
questions.correct_feedback: Slow breathing can help Nico pause and settle before deciding what to do next.

areas.world_action: Guide Nico through a short paced-breathing interaction.
areas.world_result: Nico’s tension meter lowers, the red glow fades in Signal Garden, and Wellness Symbol 1 appears.
areas.story_source: Nico is waiting for the delayed festival program. His shoulders are tight, his stomach feels uncomfortable, and he keeps saying that everything will go wrong.

areas.title: Plan Path
areas.story: The learner breaks the delayed festival task into realistic steps and chooses a trusted person and respectful way to ask for help. The player applies the plan through an in-world action and restores the support route, revealing Wellness Symbol 2.

opening_dialogue.speaker: Health Guide Aya
opening_dialogue.text: A large task can feel smaller when it is divided into clear steps.

opening_dialogue.speaker: Health Guide Aya
opening_dialogue.text: Help Maya choose one first step and identify a trusted person who can answer questions.

learning_clues: Break a large task into small, realistic steps.
Asking a trusted adult, teacher, or responsible helper is a healthy coping action.

questions.prompt: Which is the best first step?

options.text: Choose one small task, such as finishing the sign title.
Try to do all tasks at exactly the same time.
Wait until the problem becomes worse.

questions.first_wrong_hint: Pick one specific and manageable action.
questions.second_wrong_explanation: Starting with one small task makes the plan easier to follow.
questions.correct_feedback: Starting with one small task makes the plan easier to follow.

questions.prompt: Who is an appropriate trusted helper at the festival?

options.text: The assigned teacher or event coordinator
A stranger who asks for private information
Anyone online who sends a message
A person who tells Maya to hide the problem

questions.first_wrong_hint: Choose someone responsible and known in the setting.
questions.second_wrong_explanation: The teacher or coordinator is an appropriate trusted helper.
questions.correct_feedback: The teacher or coordinator is an appropriate trusted helper.

questions.prompt: Which request is assertive and respectful?

options.text: “I feel overwhelmed. Can you help me choose what to do first?”
“I will not tell anyone what is wrong.”

questions.first_wrong_hint: Use clear feelings and a specific request.
questions.second_wrong_explanation: The statement explains the concern and asks for practical help.
questions.correct_feedback: The statement explains the concern and asks for practical help.

questions.prompt: A coping plan can include both small steps and support from a trusted person.
questions.first_wrong_hint: Healthy coping can combine self-management and help-seeking.
questions.second_wrong_explanation: The statement is true.
questions.correct_feedback: The statement is true.

areas.world_action: Arrange Maya’s tasks into three steps and walk with her to the event coordinator.
areas.world_result: The route signs align, Maya begins calmly, and Wellness Symbol 2 appears.
areas.story_source: Maya is overwhelmed because she must prepare a sign, practice a line, and find the meeting point before the festival begins. She does not know where to start.

areas.title: Rest Grove
areas.story: The learner balances sleep, movement, recreation, quiet time, and support in a simple daily coping plan, then applies the complete plan to the original festival problem. Wellness Park shifts from red to calm green, Wellness Symbol 3 appears, and the mission completes.

opening_dialogue.speaker: Health Guide Aya
opening_dialogue.text: One coping strategy may help, but a balanced plan gives several safe choices.

opening_dialogue.speaker: Health Guide Aya
opening_dialogue.text: Build a simple plan the children can use now and later.

learning_clues: Healthy coping may include rest, hydration, movement, recreation, quiet time, and support.
Choose strategies that are safe, available, and appropriate to the situation.

questions.prompt: Select two healthy actions for the waiting period.

options.text: Keep worries secret from every trusted adult.

questions.first_wrong_hint: Choose actions that safely support body and mind.
questions.second_wrong_explanation: Hydration and a quiet break are safe coping actions.
questions.correct_feedback: Hydration and a quiet break are safe coping actions.

questions.prompt: What should the learner do if strong stress continues or feels unsafe?

options.text: Tell a trusted adult and ask for help.
Leave the area alone without permission.

questions.first_wrong_hint: Persistent or serious concerns need trusted support.
questions.second_wrong_explanation: The learner should seek help from a trusted adult.
questions.correct_feedback: The learner should seek help from a trusted adult.

questions.prompt: Which plan is most balanced?

options.text: Water, a short rest, light movement, and checking in with the teacher
Only scrolling on a device for the entire delay
Ignoring body signals and practicing without breaks
Doing every task alone without rest

questions.first_wrong_hint: A balanced plan uses more than one safe strategy.
questions.second_wrong_explanation: The selected plan supports physical, emotional, and social well-being.
questions.correct_feedback: The selected plan supports physical, emotional, and social well-being.

questions.prompt: Healthy coping means every person must use exactly the same strategy.
questions.first_wrong_hint: People may need different safe strategies.
questions.second_wrong_explanation: The statement is false; safe coping choices can differ by person and situation.
questions.correct_feedback: The statement is false; safe coping choices can differ by person and situation.

areas.world_action: Assemble and apply the balanced coping plan at Rest Grove.
areas.world_result: The park changes from red to calm green, the festival group regains focus, Wellness Symbol 3 appears, and the mission completes.
areas.story_source: The festival delay continues. Nico and Maya need a balanced plan that includes rest, water, light movement, a quiet activity, and support from a trusted adult if stress remains strong.

missions.title: The Vanishing Supply Cart
missions.learning_focus: Matter has mass and occupies space; solids, liquids, and gases.
missions.story_premise: A supply cart appears empty, yet its balloon, bottle, and sealed boxes still contain matter. The player helps Lab Guide Tala prove what is present.
missions.mission_objective: Complete the three connected areas and apply the mission learning focus: Matter has mass and occupies space; solids, liquids, and gases.

areas.title: Solid and Liquid Depot
areas.story: The learner observes solid objects and pours a fixed amount of liquid into differently shaped containers. The guided investigation compares definite shape with changing container shape while showing that both occupy space. Evidence Token 1 is earned.

opening_dialogue.speaker: Lab Guide Tala
opening_dialogue.text: The cart is not empty. Start with the solid and liquid supplies.

opening_dialogue.speaker: Lab Guide Tala
opening_dialogue.text: Predict what will happen when the water changes containers, then observe and record the result.

learning_clues: A solid has a definite shape and occupies space.
A liquid takes the shape of its container and occupies space.

questions.prompt: What will happen when the same water is poured into the wide bowl?

options.text: It will take the bowl’s shape.
It will no longer occupy space.

questions.first_wrong_hint: Make a prediction from the clues already observed.
questions.second_wrong_explanation: The water changes shape to match its container.
questions.correct_feedback: The water changes shape to match its container.

questions.prompt: Which object keeps its own shape?

options.text: The empty space above the bowl

questions.first_wrong_hint: Compare the solid and liquid.
questions.second_wrong_explanation: The wooden block is a solid with a definite shape.
questions.correct_feedback: The wooden block is a solid with a definite shape.

questions.prompt: The water stops being matter when its shape changes.
questions.first_wrong_hint: Matter still occupies space even when its shape changes.
questions.second_wrong_explanation: The statement is false. The water remains matter.
questions.correct_feedback: The statement is false. The water remains matter.

questions.prompt: Which observation supports that the liquid occupies space?

options.text: The liquid fills part of each container.

questions.first_wrong_hint: Use an observation about the liquid’s volume in the container.
questions.second_wrong_explanation: Filling part of the container shows that the liquid occupies space.
questions.correct_feedback: Filling part of the container shows that the liquid occupies space.

areas.world_action: Pour the measured liquid, compare the containers, and record the observation.
areas.world_result: The solid and liquid inventory lights activate and Evidence Token 1 appears.
areas.story_source: A wooden block keeps its own shape. The same amount of colored water is poured from a tall cylinder into a wide bowl; its shape changes, but it still occupies space.

areas.title: Gas and Mass Yard
areas.story: The learner uses a balloon and sealed container to show that gas occupies space, then compares objects and containers with a guided balance. The zone connects visible and invisible matter to evidence of space and mass. Evidence Token 2 is earned.

opening_dialogue.speaker: Lab Guide Tala
opening_dialogue.text: Gas can be hard to see, so we need evidence.

opening_dialogue.speaker: Lab Guide Tala
opening_dialogue.text: Observe the balloon before and after adding air, then compare the guided balance readings.

learning_clues: Gas occupies space even when it is invisible.
Matter has mass; a guided comparison can provide evidence.

questions.prompt: What will likely happen when air is pumped into the balloon?

options.text: The balloon will turn into metal.
The air will stop occupying space.

questions.first_wrong_hint: Think about the space taken by the added air.
questions.second_wrong_explanation: The balloon expands because the gas occupies space.
questions.correct_feedback: The balloon expands because the gas occupies space.

questions.prompt: Which observation is evidence that gas occupies space?

options.text: The balloon becomes larger after air is added.
The scale sits on a table.

questions.first_wrong_hint: Look for a change caused by adding air.
questions.second_wrong_explanation: The expansion is direct evidence that gas occupies space.
questions.correct_feedback: The expansion is direct evidence that gas occupies space.

questions.prompt: Invisible gas can still be matter.
questions.first_wrong_hint: Matter does not have to be visible.
questions.second_wrong_explanation: The statement is true: gas has mass and occupies space.
questions.correct_feedback: The statement is true: gas has mass and occupies space.

questions.prompt: Why is a sealed balloon used for the balance comparison?

options.text: To keep the gas contained during the measurement
To make the balloon a solid
To remove all matter from it
To change every part of the setup

questions.first_wrong_hint: The test needs the gas to remain in the balloon.
questions.second_wrong_explanation: Keeping the gas contained makes the comparison meaningful.
questions.correct_feedback: Keeping the gas contained makes the comparison meaningful.

areas.world_action: Inflate and seal the balloon, then use the guided balance to compare the prepared samples.
areas.world_result: The gas and mass indicators activate and Evidence Token 2 appears.
areas.story_source: An uninflated balloon is small. Air from a pump inflates it, showing that gas occupies space. A sealed inflated balloon also changes the balance reading compared with the uninflated balloon.

areas.title: Classification Gate
areas.story: The learner classifies everyday examples as solid, liquid, or gas and explains one observable reason for each. The integrated final challenge restores the supply-cart inventory by identifying matter that was visible and invisible. Evidence Token 3 completes the mission.

opening_dialogue.speaker: Lab Guide Tala
opening_dialogue.text: The final gate needs a complete matter inventory.

opening_dialogue.speaker: Lab Guide Tala
opening_dialogue.text: Classify the examples and use evidence about mass and occupied space.

learning_clues: Solids keep a definite shape; liquids take the shape of their container; gases spread to fill available space.
Solids, liquids, and gases are matter because they have mass and occupy space.

questions.prompt: How should the wooden block be classified?
questions.first_wrong_hint: It keeps its own shape.
questions.second_wrong_explanation: The block is a solid.
questions.correct_feedback: The block is a solid.

questions.prompt: How should the bottled water be classified?
questions.first_wrong_hint: It takes the shape of its container.
questions.second_wrong_explanation: The water is a liquid.
questions.correct_feedback: The water is a liquid.

questions.prompt: What matter is inside the ball?
questions.first_wrong_hint: The ball expands because something fills it.
questions.second_wrong_explanation: Air is a gas and is matter.
questions.correct_feedback: Air is a gas and is matter.

questions.prompt: Which two properties support that all three examples are matter?

options.text: They all keep the same shape.

questions.first_wrong_hint: Use the mission’s two defining properties.
questions.second_wrong_explanation: Matter has mass and occupies space.
questions.correct_feedback: Matter has mass and occupies space.

areas.world_action: Classify the three supplies and restore them to the correct cart compartments.
areas.world_result: The inventory gate opens, the cart is restored, Evidence Token 3 appears, and the mission completes.
areas.story_source: The restored cart contains a wooden block, bottled water, and an air-filled ball. The learner must classify each item and explain how the evidence shows that all three are matter.
